Our Vision and Values

Parents/Carers
Working in partnership with parents and carers is vital to our students. We know this can be daunting, especially when considering Post-16 options.
Here are some tips for parents/carers on how to support with careers education at home:
Read through the sections on the website to ensure that you are informed about what is going on in school and what information is available to you
Create your own Unifrog account and use it to browse courses, subjects, careers. You can even take your own personality, interests and work-related quizzes! (see below)
Browse the useful websites section of the website.
Have conversations at home. Ask your child about their interests, their futures and what options they are considering. Explore with them, be curious and show that you are interested.
Talk to us – contact us via info@wsfg.waltham.sch.uk if you have any questions or concerns
Unifrog
WSFG have bought into an incredibly valuable tool called 'Unifrog' This is a one stop careers advice station. It is your daughter’s tool to access information on colleges, universities, careers and qualifications. Students can keep their profile up to date and get advice on their next steps. They can add activities to their ‘locker’ to build a portfolio which can support with CV writing, college and job applications. Students’ logins will stay in place even once they have left WSFG provided we are still with 'Unifrog'. Ask your daughter to show you this tool at home and encourage them to update it regularly.
Volunteer With Us! Careers Education at Walthamstow School for Girls.
At Walthamstow School for Girls, we are committed to providing a thorough, broad and rich careers education for our students with as many encounters as possible with volunteers from the world of work. We want students to be well-equipped to make important decisions about their future careers and pathways.
We couldn't do this without the generosity of people like you and I want to thank you in advance for working closely with our school.
If you are able to volunteer for one or more events, please complete the questionnaire linked below. This is an expression of interest, not a full commitment. As we approach specific events, we will reach out to you to confirm your availability.
https://forms.office.com/e/Sj6MKvwbrc

Year 9 Latin Trip to St Albans
The Year 9 Latin students enjoyed a glorious day in St Albans.
In the morning they explored the Verulamium museum and had the opportunity to handle and interpret artefacts that have lain in the ground for over 2,000 years.
After enjoying lunch in the beautiful St Albans park, they walked to the ancient cathedral and spent the afternoon there making their own mosaics, inspired by ancient Roman designs.
Ms Cheetham
I really enjoyed it! It was very informative and a nice break from being stuck in the classroom all day. I especially liked being able to wander around the museum myself, so I could just stop to read a sign whenever, and making the mosaics, which was super cool. I definitely think this would be a great experience for future years. Thanks for the fun day! Laurel 8C

pageCache.text:
Year 10 Geography Field Trip
Shortly after half term, the Humanities faculty arranged for our 50 year 10 geographers to take a visit to the seaside at Walton on the Naze.
The purpose of the trip was for students to be able to see first-hand the landscape they had been studying as part of their GCSE geography topic on coasts, and consider the different ways that people have tried to manage the issue of erosion and flooding.
During the day, students carried out a variety of fieldwork techniques which allowed them to conduct an investigation into how successful the local coastal management strategies had been.
We were extremely impressed with the mature attitude students adopted in completing this work, and they all returned to school with a wealth of data allowing them to write up their final fieldwork reports. This will provide a fantastic foundation for the demands of their paper 3 next summer when they eventually come to sit their GCSE exams.
Of course, it wouldn't have been a day at the seaside without an opportunity to have an ice-cream and some fun on the beach and we had plenty of time for this also thanks to the fantastic work ethic of our students.
Mr Sterlini Head of Humanities

Year 10 Textiles Artist Workshop
Year 10 Textile students worked alongside Artist Emily Jo Gibbs, for an inspiring and mindful textiles workshop. Emily came into school and kindly shared her experiences as a practising textile artist. She talked about her influences, going to university and the twists and turns her career has taken since designing and making decorative evening bags for clients worldwide.
Emily teaches and currently creates hand-stitched portraits and still lifes with a graphic quality. She has just completed a yearlong artist’s residency at Trinity Buoy Wharf. Emily has received significant critical acclaim and examples of her work are in The Victoria and Albert Museum, The Crafts Council Collection and The Museum of Fine Art, Houston. She is a member of Contemporary Applied Arts, The 62 Group of Textile Artists, and the Artworkers Guild.
Emily has developed a beautiful and delicate technique using layers of silk organza and hand applique. The workshop centred around this technique; Emily shared this technique, her knowledge and her love of textiles with our students.
This is what the students had to say ...
It was amazing to meet an artist who has a successful career in textile art. I learnt an exciting new technique that I can apply to my coursework – Betty
It was a lovely experience, and I learnt a new applique technique - Hailey
It was a very interesting and enjoyable experience; I will be using this technique in my own work in the future – Iris
The workshop was fun, and I hope we can do another workshop with Emily as she was friendly, and hand stitching is relaxing - Hajrah and Hanifa
The workshop not only aimed to increase students’ appliquéing skills, but more importantly to inspire our future textiles artists, thank you Emily, it certainly did!
Ms. Healy Textiles Teacher

2026 GCSE Results success!
The results are in ...
Year 11 students at Walthamstow School for Girls returned to collect their GCSE results, welcomed by the Headteacher, Senior Leadership Team and many supportive teachers.
This year’s results continue to demonstrate strong progress and achievement at WSFG, with 66% of students achieving a grade 5 or above in English and Maths. Overall performance remains strong, with 64% of students achieving 5 or more GCSEs at grade 5 or above, including English and Maths, and 81% achieving grade 4 or above.
Among this year’s high achievers are:
EM: 9 grades 7–9, including 7 grade 9s. She will study Maths, Further Maths, Physics and English Literature at Harris Academy, Westminster.
HR: 10 grades 7–9, including eight grade 9s. She will study at LAE Tottenham.
LS: 9 grades 7–9, including six grade 9s. She plans to study Biology, Psychology and Sociology at LASWAP.
LL: 9 grades 7–9, including six grade 9s.
When asked what advice they would give to next year’s Year 11 students, the Year 11s encouraged them to stay focused, work consistently, make time to enjoy themselves and, above all, have confidence in themselves.
The Headteacher remarked:
“We are incredibly proud of all our students and the achievements they have made. A huge thank-you goes to our dedicated staff, who have worked tirelessly to support Year 11 throughout their time at WSfG, and to our parents/carers and families for their continued encouragement and support. Our students’ success is truly the result of a strong community working together.
“Today is an opportunity to celebrate not only academic achievement, but also the personal growth and development of our students during their time at WSfG. They are a remarkable group of young women who have demonstrated courage, compassion, creativity and determination.
“I wish all our students every success as they begin the next chapter of their educational journeys. We look forward to hearing about all they achieve and the exciting opportunities that lie ahead.”

Stage4Change at the Soho Theatre
I wanted to share an exciting opportunity for young people across Waltham Forest through Stage4Change, a free youth theatre programme that I founded alongside my previous role as a Social Worker and current role as a Functional Family Therapist. This term we have very excitingly been offered the opportunity to perform at Soho theatre in Walthamstow this Christmas and we are looking for more young people to take part!
Stage4Change was created to provide creative opportunities for young people supported by Children's Social Care and Early Help services. Through theatre, storytelling, and performance, the project aims to build confidence, develop communication skills, encourage positive peer relationships, and give young people a platform to express themselves in a supportive environment.
We are currently recruiting young people aged 11-18 to join us as we work towards our performance, Our Voice, at Soho Theatre Walthamstow on 10 December.
This is a genuinely unique opportunity for young people to collaborate with a nationally recognised theatre organisation and perform in one of Waltham Forest's most significant new cultural venues! Access to professional theatre spaces and creative industries can often feel out of reach for many of the young people we support, making this a rare and valuable opportunity to be part of something special.
No previous theatre experience is required, and all sessions are completely free.
Rehearsals Thursdays, 5pm-7pm Walthamstow Queens Road Family Hub
I would be incredibly grateful if colleagues could share the attached flyer with any young people, families, carers, or practitioners who may know someone who would benefit from this opportunity.
Tickets for Our Voice will be going on sale soon, and it would be wonderful to see colleagues from Children's Social Care, Early Help, Family Support and wider services in the audience. The show will be a celebration of the creativity, commitment, and talent of the young people involved, and I know their confidence would be hugely boosted by seeing professionals who have supported them come along and cheer them on.
